mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is declining, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% for three consecutive months, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and dampens corporate earnings growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for 3 months, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate and an increase in the federal funds rate indicates a tight labor market with rising monetary policy, which typically leads to higher inflation expectations and reduced equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: labor market tightness with monetary tightening
failure_condition: The joint signal of UNRATE decline and FEDFUNDS rise fails to predict negative returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion, high consumer spending as measured by retail sales (RSAFS) and strong housing starts (HOUST) signal robust economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings continue to rise.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of late-cycle expansion periods despite high RSAFS and HOUST, or the Rank IC for the combined signal is below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS is rising, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over 2-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100 for two consecutive months, it signals a contraction in manufacturing output that reduces corporate profitability and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 100 for 2 months, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over 2-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a broad-based economic slowdown in both the housing sector and manufacturing, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced economic activity and lower corporate earnings.
failure_condition: The joint signal of HOUST decline and INDPRO decline fails to predict negative returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a rising federal funds rate combined with a declining GDP growth rate (GDPC1) signals a contractionary policy that suppresses economic activity, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of monetary tightening cycles when FEDFUNDS is rising and GDPC1 is declining, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over 3-year windows.
